title: How would you estimate the size of the UK gym membership market?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How big is the UK gym membership market each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A good one for practising sanity checks, because the real market turns out to be bigger than this estimate, and the reason is instructive. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How big is the UK gym membership market each year?

The approach

People × share with a membership × monthly fee × 12.

Tip: When you finish, say what the number means for the client, not just the number.

Step by step

  1. People in the UK: 68M
  2. × 15% have a gym membership
  3. × £35 average monthly fee
  4. × 12 months

That gives about £4.28B a year.

Does it make sense?

About 10 million members at budget-to-mid prices; budget chains pull the average fee down.

Real-world check

Industry reports for 2025 to 2026 put UK gym membership at about 12 million people (around 18% of the population) and the market at roughly £6.5 to £7.3 billion. The estimate lands lower mainly because premium clubs pull the real average fee up. That is the value of a sanity check: it shows which assumption to revisit.

Source: Health Club Management: UK fitness market data.
